chapter: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
title: Grand Central Hotel, the Booker T. Washington Theater and cutting contests
summary: Thomas describes the Turpin brothers' theater, the late-night cutting contests at the Grand Central, and the St. Louis trumpeters he met there, calling it a trumpet town.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: JT (2 of 1) 61

Now the Grand Central is right up the street from the Booker T. Washington Theater. The Booker T. Washington Theater was run by some fellows by the name of, owned by Tom and Ben Turpin who I found out (today)-- tremendous people ...
Big ragtime piano player, wasn't he?

Better believe it. So I didn't know anything about that and I didn't think about it at all, nothing like that, you know. But, I'd go by this hotel and they had little sessions at night. They had cutting contests. That's what they called them in those days, cutting contests, you know.
Yes, jam sessions.
No, no, cutting contests.
That's a different thing?
Oh, it's a different thing altogether.
You mean this is serious.

Oh, yeah, this is you know and it's for free. It's the damnedest thing I ever heard in the world, it's for free but it certainly was. But, we did. So they did digged it. So I would go down and listen to the guys. So a fellow by the name of Crock Stanley Stanley of Walter (Scratch) Sandy, always think about him, you know. I was just thinking about him today. Say, "Here comes the country boy." Johnny Bugs, he used to work for Fats Waller, Johnny Hamilton, yeah, we worked together out in North and South Road, you know. That's when I first met him.
JT (2 of 1) 62
He was from St. Louis, too?
Oh, yeah.
That's a real trumpet town.
It was a trumpet town. It was very much a trumpet town.
Was that other guy Sleepy Tomlin or something?
Sleepy, yeah, a good buddy. Beautiful trumpet player.
He was from St. Louis?
Yeah. I met him in St. Louis. Beautiful trumpet player. James Oliver Cobb, Baby Jane, I don't remember all.
Was Shorty about your age?

Shorty Baker? No, Shorty's younger. Beautiful trumpet player. That's a funny thing that happened. It's around '28, too. There's a cab driver. So, ... I go to jam sessions. I made out all right. Of course, I had some ideas of what to do.
